Market corrections are a regular phenomenon:

The US equity market has recorded an average of 1 correction of 10%+ per year since 1930.

Since 2000, the S&P 500 has seen 24 regular corrections.

Despite these declines, the S&P 500 has delivered positive annual returns in 19 calendar years since 2000.

Furthermore, US stocks have posted 3.4 pullbacks of 5%+ per year on average since 1930.

By comparison, a bear market has occurred once every 3.3 years on average over the same period.

Market corrections are a natural feature of equity markets.
